patch_description: The current program is slow (7.12s) because it evaluates candidate perturbations one at a time with a Python-level triple loop. The prior faster programs show that vectorizing candidate evaluation is the key to both speed and quality: with a batched best-of-K move we can afford many more restarts and a finer multi-scale step schedule within the same wall time, which directly improves min_area (the primary objective). Additionally, focusing moves on the points of the K worst triplets (rather than only the single worst) helps escape poor basins. I therefore: (1) add `_areas_all` and a `_min_area_batch` helper, (2) replace the scalar inner loop with a vectorized best-of-24 perturbation over the movers of the 6 worst triplets plus a fallback global sweep, and (3) increase restarts to 25 with early bail-out on hopeless starts so time budget is spent on good basins.
